---
# TEMPLATE: collection of YouTube recordings (talks, webinars, conference sessions, recorded courses)
# Copy this whole folder into books_training/, rename the folder, and fill in the fields below.
#
# As well as this page, a recordings collection needs a few more steps - see
# "Adding YouTube recordings" > "Adding a new collection" in the main README.md:
#   1. add the collection to resources/recordings/collections.yml, with folder: books_training/<your folder name>
#   2. add the entry to the Sources list at the bottom of recordings/index.qmd
#   3. fetch and build the recordings (or ask a maintainer to run the GitHub Action for you)
#
# Lines starting with # are comments - you can leave them in or delete them.

title: "Replace this with the name of the collection, e.g. 'Community Name: Conference Recordings'"

categories:
  - Courses and Training or Reference Materials
  # Keep ONE of these options:
  - Recorded Talks  # talks, webinars and conference recordings
  # - Courses       # recorded training courses or workshops that can be followed at your own pace...
  # - Asynchronous  # ...in which case keep both Courses and Asynchronous, and delete Recorded Talks

tool-language: # The language(s) the recordings are mostly about, or N/A for a mix.
  - N/A

status: 'N/A' # Collections from many different presenters aren't rated as a whole.

image: my_image.png # Image for the listing card and the top of the entry, e.g. the channel banner or a still from a talk.
                    # Put it in this folder and give just its filename. If you don't have one, delete this line.

author: # The community or organisation that publishes the recordings.
  - name: Community or Organisation Name

date: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00" # REQUIRED: when the entry was added or last updated, e.g. "2026-01-31T10:00:00+00:00".
                                  # Used to order the homepage's "Most recently added or updated" list. Don't use `today` or `last-modified`.

pub-info:
  # Icon shown after the title: fa-hospital for NHS/healthcare organisations, fa-user-graduate for academia.
  # If neither applies, delete the project-type line.
  project-type: <i class="fa-solid fa-hospital"></i>
  rationale-for-status: |
    Collection of recordings from many different presenters, so it is not ranked as a whole.
  entry-author: # Optional: you, the person writing this Atlas entry. Delete this block if you'd rather not be named.
    - name: Your Name
      url: https://github.com/your-username
  abstract: | # Summary shown on the listing card and at the top of the entry. Aim for 50-200 words.
    Replace this with a short description of the recordings: who publishes them, which events they're from, and the topics they cover.
  links:
  - name: YouTube
    url: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
    icon: fa-brands fa-youtube
  - name: Website
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-globe

# The table of talks. talks.yml is created in this folder by resources/scripts/build_youtube_talks.py - don't edit it by hand.
# If the collection has more than one playlist, you can add `event` to `fields` (and to filter-ui and sort-ui)
# to show each playlist's label, and use `sort: false` to keep the order from collections.yml.
listing:
  - id: talk-recordings
    contents: talks.yml
    type: table
    fields: [title, year, duration, description]
    field-display-names:
      title: "Talk"
      year: "Year"
      duration: "Duration"
      description: "Details"
    sort: "date desc"
    filter-ui: [title, year, description]
    sort-ui: [title, year, duration]
    page-size: 25
---

## Search the talks

Search for a talk by title, speaker, year or topic. Newest recordings are listed first.

*Last checked against YouTube on {{< meta recordings-checked >}} - the recordings are checked every week.*

::: {#talk-recordings}
:::

You can also browse the full [playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx) on YouTube.

To search these recordings alongside talks, webinars and workshops from other communities, use the [Recordings Finder](/recordings/index.qmd).
